items.why: Today the index physically cannot express 'has an Altium footprint'. It is single-tool, single-asset, and rebuilt from scratch every sync.

steps.t: Incremental sync, no DROP TABLE
steps.evidence: No DROP TABLE anywhere in _SCHEMA (asserted by a test), every object IF NOT EXISTS, and sync() upserts by comparing a sha256 of each record file's BYTES against a stored source_hash. CONTENT, not mtime: a 'touch' must not count as a change, and this repo has already shipped a bug from treating an mtime as one. Both directions tested - a touched but unchanged file parses 0 records, and an edit that keeps the same length still parses 1 (which a size-or-mtime check would miss). Removal is explicit: a record file that disappears has its parts row AND its child rows deleted, which the old full-rebuild got for free by dropping everything and an incremental path has to do on purpose. ctx.rebuild_index() now calls sync() instead of close+rebuild. 4 mutations run, all caught.

steps.t: Measured before/after on a synthetic 10k library
steps.evidence: MEASURED on a synthetic 10,000-record library. Cold build (parse all 10k) 0.50s. sync with nothing changed: 0.14s, 10000 unchanged / 0 PARSED. sync after ONE edit: 0.14s, 9999 unchanged / 1 parsed. So a library write went from re-parsing 10k records to parsing 1 - a 3.7x wall-clock win, NOT the 100x the parse saving alone suggests, because the residual 0.14s is reading and hashing all 10k files and I am not claiming otherwise. Also measured: search 29ms, facets 1.9ms, parts_missing_asset(altium,footprint) 5.4ms over 10k - the last being a query that was impossible before.

steps.t: Expresses TRUST, not just presence
steps.evidence: part_assets stores origin_vendor/origin_url/origin_captured_at and checks_json - the raw CHECK FACTS. NO VERDICT COLUMN EXISTS (asserted by a test reading PRAGMA table_info). asset_trust() derives PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN through model.trust.verdict_for on every read, so tightening a check re-judges the library with no re-audit. UNKNOWN for an unmeasured asset, never a pass. assets_by_origin() counts unattributed assets under '(unrecorded)' rather than dropping them, because 'we do not know where this came from' is the answer the owner's complaint ('its not trusted where we've gotten them') most needs. Mutation-proven: returning a fixed verdict fails 2 tests.

steps.t: Search, facets and parametric filters still green
steps.evidence: 693 store + api tests pass unchanged (search, facets, duplicates, parametric filters, completion rollup), plus an explicit test that the public read API - count/search/facets/find_by_mpn/get - behaves identically. The schema changed underneath; the contract did not.

items.name: Cold-Eyes Review, Verified And Fixed
items.why: An independent review of the diff (07db6a8..6d27dba) found 11 real defects, most with a mutation proving they were real and a negative control proving the check was not vacuous. All 11 were fixed in the same session and re-verified with the same mutation.

steps.t: Finding 1 (CRITICAL): fetch_payload used HTTP-truthiness ('ok' if body else 'not_found') to decide a hit, but a genuine not-found is HTTP 200 with an EMPTY results list - a truthy dict. A fabricated MPN was indistinguishable from a real hit: written to sourced/, indexed, counted imported, and never retried.
steps.evidence: mouser.py + digikey_api.py fetch_payload now parse the body the same way lookup() already did correctly. Re-ran the reviewer's exact negative control: real hit -> ok/not-None, ZZZNOTAREALPART123 -> not_found/None, on BOTH adapters. 4 new regression tests in tests/backend/enrich/{test_mouser,test_digikey_api}.py.

steps.t: Finding 2: the writer-check's own 'can it fail' test built a synthetic AST from a string and asserted ast.walk() finds a call in it - testing the ast module, not the gate. MEASURED to be vacuous: disabling the real gate left it green.
steps.evidence: Split engine.assert_no_writer_imported into _scan_modules_for_writes(modules, writer), callable directly. Rewrote the self-test to drive it against an injected temp module with a real write_payload() call PLUS a negative control (a clean module must not raise). Reproduced the reviewer's exact mutation (disable the gate) -> now correctly FAILS; restored -> green.

steps.t: Finding 3 (CRITICAL): the DetailPanel's own 'Add X to make this part usable' line hardcoded symbol/footprint/3D-model regardless of part_class, recreating the exact class-blindness bug edaTarget.ts fixed - one layer up, in the same session.
steps.evidence: missingAssets now derives from kicad.missing (already class-aware); hasModel's stock-3D inheritance narrowed from 'any class needing no owned model' to 'passive specifically' (a mechanical footprint is not guaranteed to carry a baked-in 3D body the way a KiCad stock passive footprint is). Drove the reviewer's exact 4-row reproduction table against the REAL RENDERED DOM: all 4 passed after the fix, 3 of 4 FAILED against the pre-fix code (mutation-proven). 4 permanent tests added to DetailPanel.test.tsx; first version of those tests was itself vacuous (canComplete gate never enabled) and caught before being trusted.

steps.t: Finding 4: an exception anywhere in one part's import could kill the WHOLE pass. UnknownNamingScheme subclasses Exception not ValueError so it escaped the catch tuple; a per-source fetch was not wrapped in any try at all.
steps.evidence: Fetch loop now catches Exception per-source (result.errors); the write/derive/reclassify catch widened from a hand-picked tuple to Exception (BaseException still uncaught). 2 regression tests: a raising fetcher across 3 parts still produces a report covering all 3; a bad --scheme fails only that part, never the batch.

steps.t: Finding 5: a payload written then a failure BEFORE the record was persisted left orphaned evidence that resumability (file-existence-based, by design) would never retry - permanently, silently, in the skipped bucket forever.
steps.evidence: import_part now detects files present but absent from record.sources ('orphaned'), indexes them WITHOUT re-fetching, and re-derives. 2 regression tests: recovery happens with a fetcher that raises if called at all (proves no re-fetch); a second pass after recovery is a clean SKIPPED.

steps.t: Finding 6: sources.py's docstring claimed a drift gate (tests/backend/importer/test_source_registry.py) that did not exist.
steps.evidence: Wrote the real file: fetch/parse registries must name the same sources, in the same relative priority order, plus a self-test that the drift logic can fail (feeds it a deliberately broken pair).

steps.t: Finding 7: load_payloads swallowed an invalid-v3-id ValueError as 'no evidence', so rederive() (a public entry point) could silently BLANK a record's derived block instead of refusing loudly.
steps.evidence: load_payloads now raises loudly for an invalid id; import_part's own id check moved to the top of the function, UNCONDITIONAL on --refetch (previously only checked in the non-refetch branch, so --refetch on a bad id would have spent real API quota before failing).

steps.t: Finding 8: pace() iterated a set (nondeterministic order) and ran for every record regardless of whether it needed a fetch - throttling a resumed pass for work it was never going to do.
steps.evidence: usable is now sorted(); pacing gated on _needs_a_fetch() per record. Regression test: a fully-imported part triggers zero pace() calls; a fresh part still triggers one (negative control).

steps.t: Finding 9: the electrical veto's whole-word matching had NO trailing \b on all but the last alternative, so 'led' matched inside 'ledge' and 'gate' inside 'Gateway' - the exact substring-matching failure the module's own thesis warns against.
steps.evidence: Every alternative now closes with its own \b. Verified: 'Aluminium ledge bracket' and 'Gateway enclosure' now correctly match their sibling controls ('Steel bracket', 'Enclosure') instead of being wrongly excused to component.

steps.t: Finding 10: the writer-check's FORBIDDEN_CALLS included bare 'replace'/'rename' attribute names, which collide with str.replace/Path.replace - a latent false-positive machine waiting for the first text.replace() in the derive path.
steps.evidence: Narrowed to {unlink, rmtree} only, neither a name any object in this path's real vocabulary (str, dict, dataclass) exposes.

steps.t: Finding 11: dead `import sys` in derive/engine.py (invisible to ruff, F401 is globally ignored by design), and a comment pointing at lib/partFields.ts, which was never created.
steps.evidence: import removed; comment corrected to state reality (detail.derived.<field>, no dedicated helper module exists).

steps.t: Categories the review checked and found CLEAN: no existing test was weakened (assertion/case counts equal or higher in every rewritten file, exactly 3 expect() lines strengthened not deleted); no blanket find/replace damage to dev-ids/comments/string literals; no consumer reads a field that no longer exists at runtime.
steps.evidence: Reported by the reviewer with counts per file; independently re-verified via full suites (backend 3513 passed/5 skipped, frontend 1260 passed, tsc clean, build clean, ruff clean) after all 11 fixes landed.

steps.t: Rewrite every reference to a renamed id (index, projects, assign bindings)
steps.evidence: Every persisted reference enumerated by READING the library, not assuming. MOVED: parts/<id>.json (158) and datasheets/<id>.pdf (85 of 158 - measured: all 85 named exactly <id>.pdf, zero other conventions) with record.datasheet.file updated in the same pass -> 0 dangling datasheet refs after. NOT TOUCHED, each checked: models/ (named by MPN, zero refs embed an id), symbols/ + footprints/ (per-CATEGORY libs), the SQLite index (derived, rebuilt), altium/*.DbLib (regenerated + gitignored). steps.evidence: Collision detection refuses rather than merging: two records mapping to one id would DESTROY one, so it is a blocking error naming both. Also refuses a filename that disagrees with the record's id (picking a winner is not a migration's call) and a record with no MPN (the id is slug(mpn)+sha256(mpn)[:4], so there is nothing to compute). Verified on the real library: 0 collisions, 0 path-UNSAFE ids afterwards (was 84 of 158), 0 filename/id disagreements. 17 tests; 5 mutations run, all caught - dropping collision detection, unlinking before writing, forgetting the datasheet ref, forgetting the id update, accepting a filename mismatch.

Backup is git itself: the library is a git repo, so a clean tree + recorded HEAD is a complete verified undo (git checkout . && git clean -fd, printed on success). REFUSES to apply against a DIRTY library tree because git is then no longer a full undo - and that check is SCOPED to the library path, after finding that a bare git status reported the whole repo's churn and would have made --allow-dirty the normal way to run it. steps.t: A pull clears untracked files an incoming commit would add
steps.evidence: GitRepo._clear_untracked_blockers: fetches, then moves aside only the paths the incoming commits ADD (--diff-filter=A) that are untracked locally. Reproduces the owners exact abort in a two-clone fixture and fixes it.

steps.t: A local file that DIFFERS is kept, never overwritten
steps.evidence: A local file whose git hash differs from the incoming blob is MOVED to .stockroom-kept keeping its path, never deleted. TAMPER-PROVEN: replacing the move with an unlink fails the test.

steps.t: An untracked file the update does not touch is left alone
steps.evidence: NARROWNESS. Only ADDED paths are touched; a bystander untracked file is untouched and no rescue dir is created. Added because a tamper widening the filter broke NOTHING in 51 tests.

steps.t: A real conflict still reports honestly
steps.evidence: NEGATIVE CONTROL: a genuine same-file divergence still returns ok=False and updated=False, so clearing blockers cannot turn a real conflict into a silent success.

steps.t: Verified on the owner's laptop
steps.evidence: BLOCKED EXTERNAL ACCEPTANCE. The exact untracked-blocker behavior is fixture-proven, but the owner's second physical Windows laptop is unavailable in this session. It must be deliberately placed behind with the historical blocker and observed recovering without a manual Git repair.
